title: Enabled META and ALT keys to work in Emacs by making them send Escape
body: I tried your addon and it is fantastic. The only issue I had is I wanted to run Emacs within the terminal but the M-<key> combinations were not working, so I have made a small update to make the META and ALT keys send an Escape to resolve that issue.
author: MichaelBScott

comments.body: I took a look at the change and I think this is on the right path, but what other terminals do is set a config option for this kind of behavior or react to an escape code being sent.  The libtmt library only did things that matches what an ANSI term type would do, but I have since extended that because it was inadequate for MS windows.  If emacs sends an escape code to have an escape sent for meta, ten I'd prefer to react to that.  Btw were you using emacs on Linux or Windows?

Thank you for the info, it sounds like it needs a more complete solution. The change I made was based on how to resolve the same issue when using XTerm by setting:

 XTerm.vt100.metaSendsEscape: true

Additionally, since pushing that change I have also determined CTRL doesn't quite fully work either. C-/ ended up writing the / character instead of performing the action for the keybinding.

Oh, and I am using Linux.

I'm not sure there is really any downside to how you made the change since I'm not sure when or why you might accidentally send an escape by just pressing the alt or meta keys, but since xterm made it configurable I'm leaning to adding that to the GDTerm settings.

BTW the Ctrl-/ is broken and I'll add an issue.  The range in the Godot key didn't match for the characters '/' and '~' so that's why that's not working.

I'm not really an emacs user, but I loaded it onto my system and will do a few tests as well.

BTW when I tried to use 'emacs -nw' on my Ubuntu system it did not behave well until I changed the TERM environment variable to "xterm-256color", so I tested it in my standard Gnome Terminal and it didn't behave well with that TERM either.

The library I used (libtmt) doesn't really attempt to do a full TERM=xterm-256color terminal emulation but it is apparently close enough that when using emacs it seemed to behave much better.  Not sure why.  It may be that emacs did some things that weren't quite compatible with a terminal as primitive as TERM=ansi.
I merged a change for Ctrl-/ but you will need to merge your updates and compile from source to check them out.

Hi @markeel,
I have built the version using your latest changes from the main branch and as far as I can tell emacs is now fully working with the Send ALT Meta as ESC option selected.

C-/ is now performing the correct action for the keybinding.
Also, setting TERM=xterm-256-color seems to work correctly for me.

This pull request is no longer required so I am closing it.

Thank you so much for your help.

> Hi @markeel, I have built the version using your latest changes from the main branch and as far as I can tell emacs is now fully working with the Send ALT Meta as ESC option selected.

title: Fixes #17: customizable shell path
body: This PR is an attempt at fixing #17 and adding customizable shell executables. This PR is currently a draft because I'm having trouble getting it to compile on Windows on account of a seemingly unrelated error (error: variable 'CreateSyntheticPointerDevice' definition is marked dllimport).
author: abstractionfactory

comments.body:
My initial reaction is that for Linux the SHELL environment variable is completely suitable.  A Linux user will set the SHELL to what they want and do not need to set it in the editor preferences.

For Windows I don't think there is an equivalent to a generally recognized environment variable for a "shell" as there is in Linux, so having an editor setting could make sense.   Of course that makes things asymmetric, so maybe supporting both would be OK, but I'd almost rather there be a Windows environment variable (GDTERM_SHELL or even just SHELL to make it super symmetric).

I'll do a deeper look at the code in the pull request tomorrow.
@markeel I'm happy to drop the PR, adding a similar SHELL env variable would be workable on Windows too, people can set it on their systems.
I think that will be easier then, I'll reassign the issue to me and take a look at extending the windows side to use a defined SHELL variable (or cmd.exe if none is defined).
Closing as per discussion above.

title: Paste adds extra newline
body:
Hello and thank you for your work!

Currently, on Windows/CMD, the paste function seems to add an extra line break. This can be reproduced when pasting into a command-line editor, such as on a `git commit`.
author: abstractionfactory

comments.body:
I've spent some time trying to reproduce this issue and when I perform the following steps:

- From within a GDTerm window enter command such as: `dir`
- Use mouse to select some word within the line
- Right-click and select Copy
- Bring up `notepad`
- Use Ctrl-V from within notepad to paste in the word

Result:
- The word is pasted but no new-line or extra line break is added.

I've also done the reverse

- Bring up `notepad`
- Type a few words
- Select one of the words within the line
- Use Ctrl-C to copy the word
- Go to a GDTerm and right-click and select 'Paste'

Result
- The word appears without a new line

Note: If you triple-click to select a line you will get the whole line on screen which includes all the trailing spaces which ends up being really long and may look like an extra new line if pasted into an application that wraps at a line column less than your GDTerm screen width.

Can you provide a more specific scenario where this issue occurs.  For example does it only happen in a particular application?

Hey @markeel specifically, I can reproduce this as follows:

1. Create a git project with something to commit
2. `git add .`
3. `git commit`
4. Open Notepad and enter something with at least two lines and copy it into the editor git opened. (If it's vi you may have to hit `i` before you can paste.)
What editor is git opening?  Mine is set to open notepad++ and it does so in another window, so it doesn't interact with the GDTerm window
It's opening vi in the GDTerm window. The Windows Terminal does not have this behavior.

The issue appears to be that VI is expecting unix style line endings and what is being pasted is coming from a windows application with DOS style line endings.  This will require additional consideration.  I'm going to have to understand what the de facto standards are for handling this when pasting and if there needs to be a paste-raw kind of mode that will paste without converting line characters when needed.

If you just pasted the commands into a command prompt then all is well, because the CMD.exe expects a CR/LF combination, but the built-in VI within GIT does not.

I've put a pull request in to address this issue.

I believe it is as simple as converting all the CRLF to CR to match what a user would type.
When pasting, GDTerm no longer puts in an extra line, because it only sends a CR (the same as if a user and pressed the enter key).

title: Ctrl+V doesn't work
body:
Hello and thank you for your work!

Currently on Windows/CMD, hitting the <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>V</kbd> key doesn't work at all. It would be nice to implement  using this key combination. Alternatively, <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>V</kbd> would also work.
author: abstractionfactory

comments.body:
This was intentional since in the Linux world the Ctrl-V is handled by the application.  

Looking at how the CMD handles it though, it looks like there is a switch to enable Ctrl keys, which is defaulted on.  This seems like a reasonable enhancement, but should be an editor level flag so that if the main purpose of the CLI is to SSH off to some system in the cloud, you would probably want the application on the far end to process the Ctrl-V/Ctrl-C (especially Ctrl-C since that is what is used to terminate a long running command).
Copy and Paste using the keyboard Shift-Ctrl-V/Shift-Ctrl-C is now supported in GDTerm
